item.description:
This is the last release before 1.0.0. I'm freezing the code this week to get 1.0.0 ready, so nothing new goes in, only fixes. If something in 0.4.1 doesn't work for you, open an issue on GitHub, that's what this week is for.

Your menu bar works with Shortcuts. Twelve actions get your layout, set it, move icons, show and hide them, and open Search. dimble:// links do the smaller changes from Alfred, a script or a browser (#169, #146, thanks @rebdeg and @ssbodda-powern).

More ways into Always Hidden. A middle-click on the chevron can show it, and so can its own keyboard shortcut. Both are off until you set them (#149, thanks @openforfuture).

Eleven betas went into this one. Dimble is also in Homebrew now, brew install --cask dimble. Most of the rest is fixes, for the Row's icons, Live Activities, full menu bars and full-screen apps.

New

  • Dimble has Shortcuts actions (#169, thanks @rebdeg). Get Menu Bar Layout gives back your whole layout as text, and Set Menu Bar Layout puts every icon where that text says, in one go. It also takes that text saved as a file, and the same text works on another Mac. Others move or open an icon, add or remove a separator, and show or hide the hidden icons. You can also turn reveal on hover or on click on and off, and open Search.
  • dimble:// links do the smaller changes without Shortcuts (#169). dimble://move?icon=Tailscale&to=hidden moves an icon, and there's show, show-all, hide, toggle, add-separator and remove-separator. Any web page can open a link, so links never read anything back, click an icon, change a setting or set the whole layout.
  • dimble://search?q=Tailscale opens Search with the text typed in, for Alfred and the like (#146, thanks @ssbodda-powern).
  • Middle-clicking the chevron can reveal your hidden icons (#149, thanks @openforfuture). Settings › Behavior › Reveal › "Middle-click reveals" offers Hidden and Always Hidden together, or Always Hidden on its own.
  • A keyboard shortcut shows Always Hidden alone (#149). It's in Settings › General › Shortcuts as "Show Always Hidden only". The same key puts it away.
  • A Shortcut button's icon can be picked in Settings (#162, thanks @Hydrogenxy). macOS keeps a shortcut's own icon in a folder only Full Disk Access opens, so Dimble can't show that one.
  • fn C opens Control Center while your icons are hidden (#179, thanks @mityeah). macOS ignores its own shortcut then, so Dimble opens it for you, however long you hold the keys. There's nothing to set up. I tested it on macOS 27.3.

Changed

  • The line between Hidden and Always Hidden is off unless you turn it on (#171, #149, thanks @bortolatto-creator and @openforfuture). If you liked it in 0.4.0, it's in Settings › Behavior › Reveal, "Show a line between Hidden and Always Hidden".
  • macOS 27.3's "System & App Protection Override" pill is off by default (#163, thanks @Titelive). It lists every app that can control others, so on a Mac with Dimble it's up all day. Settings › Menu Bar › Live Activities brings it back, and it shows its count now.
  • Settings › Menu Bar lists Live Activities and "Show when it matters" before App launchers and Dimble items.
  • The log says when a Time Machine backup starts and ends (#167, thanks @brianaweeks1). It's to find out why the Time Machine icon set to "While backing up" doesn't come out for everyone.

Fixed, the Row and Panel

  • The Row's icons should be sharp on every screen (#156, thanks @avocadoattack). Dimble took every picture from the main display, so with a 1x display as main the MacBook's Row was scaled up and fuzzy. Each screen now draws pictures from a bar of its own scale. An icon with no sharp picture shows the app's icon instead. On MacBooks whose bar is taller than the notch area, the bar is read at its full height, which should also fix a panel sitting too high. I don't have that setup here, so tell me on the issue if yours still looks soft.
  • Icons in the Row sit centred in their tiles (#156). On a 1x display the bar's shadow could count as part of the icon.
  • An icon over a sharp edge in your wallpaper gets its own picture in the Row and Panel (#156). Dimble read the edge as another icon in the way and showed the app's icon instead.
  • Icons macOS parks behind its « should get their real picture (#153, thanks @2f4vwwb5t6-gif). Their tiles kept an old picture or a chevron. Old pictures are dropped once, so a few tiles show the app's icon until a new one is taken.
  • Without Screen Recording, the Row and Panel show each app's icon instead of old fragments of the bar (#156).
  • Time Machine and Dimble's other icons open their menu with the icon in the bar (#167, thanks @brianaweeks1). From the Panel, the menu opened with the bar fuzzy and the icon missing.
  • Pressing an icon in the Panel works in a full-screen app with the menu bar hidden. Docked, it also opens the right icon when macOS's « has it.
  • The Panel tab's "Show hidden icons in" works on a display that has its own choice in Settings › Displays.

Fixed, Live Activities

  • Now Playing should come back right after you resume (#156). It could take a minute, or not come back at all with every other Live Activity off. I measured it on macOS 27.3 only.
  • A Live Activity isn't drawn half-way through its slide anymore (#164, thanks @fontme).
  • The bar doesn't keep a lighter rectangle or band after the wallpaper changes (#165, thanks @fontme).
  • The pill shouldn't sit in a lighter or darker box after you move to another display (#156).
  • An Always Hidden icon that ended up among your Hidden ones stays hidden with a Live Activity up, and goes back to Always Hidden once it ends. Battery showed all through a call on a display that shows every icon, and each time you hovered to show the hidden icons. It can still flash for a second as the Live Activity starts.
  • Live mode steps aside on a display where a full-screen app has the bar (#156, thanks @avocadoattack). It stayed up as a block at the top of a full-screen video for about 13 seconds. Your other displays keep their Live Activities. When you move the pointer to the top of the full-screen display, they step aside for about 10 seconds, and the hidden icons there can show for a moment as its bar comes down.
  • The pill doesn't blink when you hover the bar, and a reveal doesn't cut it before macOS's «. Hidden icons also show when the « was left open.
  • Two Live Activities from one app keep their own content, two Sports games could swap scores. Your other displays show the same pills as the main one.
  • Old icons or a pill shouldn't stay at the left of the bar with a Live Activity up. It happened when an app launched just as Dimble took its picture of the bar. I tested it by forcing the two together, so tell me if you still see it.

Fixed, reveal and hide

  • Smooth and Fade play with a Live Activity up (#154, thanks @hanin-mohammed). Your icons came and went in one cut whatever style you'd picked. Smooth also survives a clock that changes width and quick hovers. I filmed it on macOS 27.3 only, if you're on 27.2 and the slide ends on a small jump, tell me on the issue.
  • An icon macOS keeps right of the « doesn't show twice during a reveal or a hide (#157, thanks @mr-steveryan).
  • The icons should hide after a hover reveal even when Dimble didn't see the pointer leave the bar (#162, thanks @Hydrogenxy). I couldn't make it happen here, so tell me on the issue if yours still sticks.
  • A tooltip or an open menu holds the reveal, wherever you've left the pointer (#148, thanks @openforfuture).
  • A popover's icon no longer keeps its grey highlight after the bar hides (#172, thanks @mr-steveryan).
  • A click on a menu bar app's icon right after a reveal opens its menu and leaves it open. Dimble could read it as a click on the empty bar.
  • A display's "Hides icons" or "Shows all icons" applies at once with a Live Activity up.
  • Switching the main display no longer leaves every bar on Hidden until a relaunch.
  • Show in Bar from Search brings a Hidden icon out on a display that hides it, while another display always shows Hidden.

Fixed, your layout

  • Icons out of order at a double-click go back in place (#171, thanks @bortolatto-creator). Dimble only saw it while the bar was open and couldn't anymore once it shut. Apply also reaches Hidden icons that sit behind macOS's « when Always Hidden is out.
  • Apply waits until it can read the bar. macOS can stop listing its icons for a few seconds, and an Apply in that moment dropped your changes and moved nothing.
  • A recording you hold down in Telegram doesn't stop on its own (#159, thanks @openforfuture). Dimble could move an icon while the button was held. Automatic moves wait for the button now. Settings also stays behind the app you're in when Dimble moves icons.
  • An Apply in a full-screen app no longer marks an app as one Dimble can't move.
  • When Dimble opens macOS's « to place an icon, the first click should land (#150). A button you add while the bar is full goes to its place, not behind the «.
  • A spacer keeps the width you set, and goes down to 1 pt (#155, thanks @defrilitus). It went back to 14 pt at each launch, so yours may change size with this update.
  • Dimble tells an app's unnamed icons apart. Stats puts five in the bar without names, and Dimble read them as one. Hiding one of them alone isn't possible yet, macOS hides a whole app at a time.

Fixed, stability

  • With several displays, Dimble could stop responding until you quit it. It asked macOS to watch the menu bar again at almost every reveal. It asks once per launch now, which makes the hang much less likely.
  • macOS's recording indicator shouldn't stay on after you quit Dimble. It did when Dimble quit in the middle of taking a picture of the bar. If yours is stuck, killall replayd in Terminal clears it.
  • Two Dimbles shouldn't run at once anymore. Quitting and opening it again right away could leave two.
  • The log names the app or tool that asked Dimble to quit (#130, thanks @cookie-drummer), on a line starting stop: asked to quit.

item.title: 0.4.1-beta.11
item.description:
Fixed

  • Now Playing and the other Live Activities show again while an app is full screen on another display (#156, thanks @avocadoattack). Since beta.8 a full-screen app on any display kept them off on every display. Now only the full-screen display goes without. When you move the pointer to the top of that display, they step aside for about 10 seconds. The hidden icons there can show for a moment as its bar comes down.
  • The space next to an Always Hidden icon among your Hidden ones closes with a Live Activity up. Beta.10 hid the icon but left its space blank, so your Hidden icons stood apart from the Live Activity. They're drawn moved over now, and a click on one opens the real icon.
  • That icon also goes back to Always Hidden once the Live Activity ends. Before, Dimble couldn't tell it was out of place.

The right-click menu is yours to arrange. It was getting crowded. Settings › Behavior lets you untick what you don't use and drag the rest into the order you want (thanks Jian). Settings and Quit always stay.

Three of the changes here came from @InTheManXG. Panels that open where you click, a line marking off Always Hidden, and show-all displays that follow your reveal setting. He sent all three as pull requests and let me take them the rest of the way.

Five betas went into this one. There's also a switch for each Live Activity, a list behind the Live Activities item, a cog in the panel's corner, and the camera and mic work macOS 27.3 made necessary. Dimble now works out how your macOS behaves by trying it, instead of reading its version number.

New

  • The right-click menu is yours to arrange, in Settings › Behavior (thanks Jian). Tick what it shows and drag the rows into your order. "Check for Updates…" and "Edit Menu Bar…" are on the list too, off by default. A divider goes on its own when the group above it empties. The same menu opens on the chevron, on a separator and on the empty bar.
  • Each Live Activity can be turned off on its own, in Settings › Menu Bar. The switch is kept by the name macOS gives the pill, so your choice outlives the activity, and the list stays there when nothing is running. Apple's camera and mic pill is never on that list, no switch may hide a privacy indicator.
  • A line in the bar marks where Always Hidden ends (#145, thanks @InTheManXG). It shows while those icons are out, in the menu bar and in the panel. It's drawn between the two icons either side of it, not between their slots, which isn't the same place when one is wide and its neighbour small.
  • Panels can open where you click (#135, thanks @InTheManXG). Settings › Panel › "Center on menu bar click", off by default. The chevron keeps its anchor, and a panel that's already open stays put while you aim at a tile.
  • A cog in the panel's corner opens Settings (#95, thanks @swhitlow). Settings › Panel › Settings button, off by default. The right-click menu already carries that row, and a cog drawn at rest costs a line of the panel's height whether or not you reach for it.

Changed

  • Clicking the Live Activities item opens the list of what's running, newest first, instead of bringing the pills back on its own. macOS draws two pills on the bar and no more, so the rest sit under a line that says how many it left off. The two it does draw open their own card from the list, the same as clicking the pill does.
  • The "Clock click opens Notification Center" switch is gone, the clock always opens it now. With Screen Recording there was nothing to choose, Dimble covers the bar and lets the click through. Without it, Settings › Behavior says why your hidden icons flash in and out for about half a second each time, and offers the grant there. If you had the switch off, the clock works again, with that flash until you grant Screen Recording.
  • Dimble works out what your macOS does by trying it once and remembering the answer, instead of checking which version you're on. Apple moves this behaviour in point releases, so a version check would need an update from us every time, and another one to undo it when Apple puts something back. Nothing is written down, each launch measures again.

Fixed

  • The Camera & mic item opens Apple's panel again on macOS 27.3. It opened and closed and left you in Privacy & Security. macOS renamed that pill, gave it a new id every camera session, moved its panel to another process and rebuilds it while the bar settles, so Dimble looks for it by shape now and finds it again on each try.
  • Apple's camera and mic pill stays on the bar while your icons are hidden, on 27.3. It was painted over, which is a privacy indicator gone. Dimble's own camera icon steps aside while that pill shows, rather than standing next to it, and a second frozen copy no longer sits on the concealed bar. The dot doesn't flash on and off while the pill arrives either. Apple builds that pill, throws it away, then builds it again a quarter of a second later, and Dimble read the gap as no pill at all.
  • No black edge past that pill on the cover. Dimble paints over it by repeating the column just left of it. Taking the picture lights the recording indicator, which slides the right end of the bar while the shot is going, so the column could land inside the pill and repeat its black out to the edge.
  • Two Live Activities from one app each open their own card. Two games in a sports app both call their pill the same thing, so a click on the right-hand one opened the left one's card.
  • A Live Activity's picture is no longer taken while its card is open, so the pill can't keep the open look once the card is gone. A pill whose text stopped moving gets a quick refresh instead of waiting five minutes, so a paused timer can't sit there with the wrong numbers. And one macOS couldn't read three times comes back. Locking your screen could take a pill away until the activity ended.
  • Focus, the Clock's timer, SharePlay and Live Activities keep up after macOS restarts its logging. Dimble waits a little longer each time one of those readers stops, and the wait never went back down, so after a few restarts a Focus change could land a minute late for the rest of the session.
  • A Focus that was already on before you logged in now shows on the bar (#92, thanks @juanfcocontreras). A Do Not Disturb schedule that started while the Mac was off left the Focus item blank until the Focus next changed. At that moment macOS logs nothing that names the Focus it's already in, so Dimble had nothing to read.
  • An icon you can see on the bar no longer turns up in "Didn't fit" (#137, thanks @ycl-2004). With several Spaces on one display, macOS lists a menu bar for each of them, and two of those lists gave one icon two different names at the same spot. Dimble read that as an icon too many, so it waited on a bar that was overflowing and drew the chevron for icons that were never behind it.
  • Right-clicking the menu bar no longer flashes macOS's own menu before Dimble's (#140, thanks @efilo1). Dimble wasn't taking that click, only watching for it, so Apple's one-item menu opened on the way down and Dimble's landed on top a beat later.
  • Coming back to the bar right after leaving it no longer waits half a second (#141, thanks @efilo1). The reveal was waiting on a cover picture the conceal had only just started taking, and that wait couldn't finish in time. Hovering back in cost 447–542ms instead of the usual 70.
  • A hidden item's menu opens on the click that asks for it (#142, thanks @alexandertsukanov). Dimble turns the pointer's association off so a drag can't fly across the screen. On a click it left the pointer loose from the point the click carried. An item that reads the pointer read it wherever you'd left it, and opened nothing. Dimble can also hold a picture of the bar over the real one, and that picture was taking the click meant for the item.
  • Clicking the empty bar on a display that shows every icon doesn't open a panel of the icons you're already looking at (#144, thanks @InTheManXG). The chevron there still opens Always Hidden, wherever your reveal setting puts it.
  • A live pill no longer sits on the Space you just left (#136, thanks @supryan). Switching between a full-screen app and the desktop left an opaque black capsule in the bar for 3.2 seconds. Everything repainted for the new Space except the cover, and that was rebuilt from a picture taken over the Space that had just gone.
  • A panel tile no longer carries pieces of the icon that stood there (#128, thanks @zleo-ai). Dimble cuts each icon out of a filmed strip against the same column of the empty bar. Icons move between those two shots, so a visible one could be standing in the column a hidden one was filmed in. Subtract it and its fragments end up in somebody else's tile.
  • A click in the very top-left corner opens the Apple menu without toggling a reveal with it (#147, thanks @dvrooman). The bar's topmost row answers as macOS's own window right across the width, so Dimble read a corner click as empty bar.
  • The « macOS draws for a bar that's overflowed expands when you click it (#150). Dimble holds a picture of the bar over the real one while it works, and that picture was taking the click.
  • An icon whose menu opens a wide panel stays out while the panel is up (#151). Dimble watches for the window a click opened, and it skipped any panel wider than 60% of the display. It read that as an ordinary window and put the icon away underneath.

One fix. If you run a Windows app through Wine (Steam, Crossover, Proton), Dimble could take gigabytes of memory, and your icons wouldn't hide.

Fixed

  • Dimble no longer climbs a folder path forever looking for the app behind a menu bar icon (#133, thanks @ZeLebo). Wine puts a doubled slash in the paths it writes, and the climb up one of those never reached the top. It took a core, grew by gigabytes a minute, and left your icons showing. Nothing else has changed since 0.3.4.
